summary.title: Release Management Best Practices with Feature Flags
summary.one_liner: You learn how to use release management feature flags (ring and percentage-based rollouts) and the planning, implementation, and deployment practices that keep launches low-risk.
keywords: how to roll out features gradually
takeaways: Release management flags are short-lived and should be removed once 100% of users have the feature.
Ring deployments release to successive user groups, while percentage deployments roll out randomly to growing percentages of users (e.g. 10%, 25%, 50%).
Plan flags during design, agree on naming conventions, and define a fallback value for every flag.
Test the feature with the flag both on and off, especially for schema or database changes, and track metrics before, during, and after deployment.
summary.summary: This LaunchDarkly blog post explains how feature flags support software rollouts such as early access, canary releases, and betas, limiting the blast radius of problems. It describes two deployment models: ring deployments, which release to groups in sequence (originally introduced by Jez Humble in Continuous Delivery), and percentage-based deployments, which randomly expand to larger user shares, optionally automated with rollbacks on errors or slow response times. The best practices are grouped into planning, implementation, and deployment phases, covering flag purpose, naming, testing both flag states, fallback values, metrics, and removing flags to avoid technical debt.
